Its Board of Directors holds ultimate authority to approve or reject policy recommendations. ICANN also implements approved policies through its staff and frameworks like the Consensus Policy Implementation Framework.

ICANN was created in 1998 to assume management of the Internet's domain name system (DNS) from the U.S. government, following the privatization of the Internet's technical infrastructure. This transition necessitated a governance model that balanced technical expertise with global representation, leading to the formalization of multistakeholder processes involving Supporting Organizations (SOs) and Advisory Committees (ACs) to ensure diverse perspectives in policy decisions.
